When subtitles sit over video or a camera, text gets lost in bright scenes. Turn on Background bar in the dashboard's Subtitle style (for this setlist only, the background bar in the format bar) to lay a semi-transparent band behind the text only.
• Bar shape: Fit to text (as long as the text) · Whole subtitle area (as wide as your subtitle area) · Full screen width (a broadcast lower-third band).
• Bar height is the band's top-to-bottom thickness. Raising it keeps the text size the same and only makes the band thicker (side padding works the same way). Set where the subtitles sit with Position and Distance from edge above.
• Pick a bar color from the suggested colors, or open More colors to drag-pick one or type a HEX code or RGB numbers. Opacity in More colors is the same value as 'Bar opacity'. Auto uses a white band on a white background and a black band otherwise, and flips the text color to match.
• Bar fill: Solid · Gradient (color 1 → color 2, 5 directions) · Fade one side (color → transparent, the scrim used in broadcasts). The dashboard preview shows exactly how the band looks on the current screen background.
• On a chroma key background the band is made opaque automatically so keying stays clean (fades become solid).
• You can also set it per slide via right-click → Style, and it carries over to PPTX (PPTX can't make a band that fits the text exactly, so ‘Fit to text’ is exported at the subtitle area width).
